This one is about making it easier to use, from a review of how people get around it and from
someone trying it out the way an *arr user would. It also brings 0.12.1, which wasn't released on
its own: security fixes for the web page, plus three fixes (see the end).

**Upgrading:** replace `usnfetch.exe` and start it as usual. If you open usnfetch by a name other
than `localhost`, an IP address or the computer's own name, and have no web password, set one
first (Settings → Web access), or it will turn that name away.

## Search

- **One Download button per result, and it says where it goes.** On the computer running usnfetch,
  a game that's one small file goes to your browser's downloads; from another computer it goes to
  usnfetch's download folder. A link under the button does it the other way, and a menu picks
  which build it comes from. The game's name no longer downloads anything by itself.
- **It tells you which builds it doesn't know yet.** Search knows the builds you've opened or
  downloaded. When some haven't been, it says so and offers to look inside them, one at a time.
  The catalog has the same Look inside for the builds you tick.

## Advanced mode

Settings hides what most people never touch: hash checks, parallel jobs, retries, streaming
connections, the index cache, the 7-Zip and UnRAR paths, provider priorities (until you have two
providers), a share's details, the catalog's Opened column and sort menu, memory figures and the
log on the System page. **Show advanced**, at the top of Settings, brings them all back; it's
saved in each browser. A setting you've changed stays in view anyway, marked "changed", and so
does anything that needs your attention, like 7-Zip not being found.

## The catalog

- **One Filters button** in place of a toolbar of menus: launcher, device, source, and hiding
  what's queued or done. The filters in use show as chips you can click off.
- **One health scale:** Gone, Missing, Partly missing, Found (its manifest is at your provider) and
  Verified (a sample of its files is too). It used to mix "Link OK" and "Available".
- Part of a build on disk reads "28 of 107 files on disk", not an amber "partial".
- A list pasted without a name no longer tags every entry "import".

## Activity

- The queue says how many jobs, how much is left, the speed and when it should be done.
- **The speed shows for downloads of many small files.** It read 0 B/s, with no ETA, because it
  was worked out per file and each small file was over too soon to have a speed.
- While everything is paused, there's one Resume (in the banner), and the jobs say they're
  waiting with the rest instead of each offering Pause.
- A speed limit under 1 MB/s reads in KB/s, not "0 MB/s".

## Setup and folders

- The download folder warns when its drive has less than 100 GB free, and offers the local disk
  with the most room.
- Folder names Windows can't use (`CON`, `bad:name`, a trailing dot) are refused as you type,
  in setup and in Settings, rather than failing later.

## Easier to read, and on a phone

- Every theme's lighter text, and the light themes' blue and orange, now meet the usual contrast
  for reading (4.5:1). Two console themes' buttons have dark text on a lighter blue.
- Labels belong to their settings, so screen readers name them; switches show where the keyboard
  is; a share's folders open from the keyboard; the status bar's text is a link to Activity.
- On a phone the menu wraps instead of hiding Settings and System off to the side, and the catalog,
  History and provider lists turn into cards.

## From 0.12.1

- **Other web pages can't use usnfetch.** A change has to come from its own page, as JSON. Without
  a web password it answers only to this computer's names (no DNS rebinding).
- **A share's files can't run anything:** they're served sandboxed, and web pages and scripts as
  plain text.
- **A saved provider password goes only to its server;** the 7-Zip and UnRAR paths change only on
  the computer running usnfetch; links in lists are followed only when they're web pages; and
  unpacking a share's index has limits.
- **A cut-off link is the share you already have,** not a second copy of the whole build.
- **Builds you downloaded without browsing are in Search.**
- **Not enough room is a pause, not a failure,** with Keep free on.
